newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian government mulls further confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: Italian government mulls further confidence vote.

text.p: Italy's centre-left cabinet decided on Wednesday to put a draft law on immigration to a confidence vote in the Senate (upper house) if hard-right opposition moves to delay its passage continued.
A government source said the decision to resort to a confidence vote "if the circumstances make it necessary" was taken at a meeting of the cabinet.
The draft law, designed to regularise the status of thousands of immigrants, faces a welter of blocking amendments in the upper house from the hard-right National Alliance party.
The government has a majority in the assembly but such amendments have to be discussed, severely delaying passage of legislation, unless they can be swept away by a confidence motion.
The draft law was submitted this month when short-term decree measures that gave illegal immigrants the chance to register and remain in Italy expired after 60 days.

Past governments routinely re-issued expired decrees but the Constitutional Court recently banned the practice. The ruling has forced Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government to use a string of confidence votes to get pending legislation passed.
